walls.notes: West tower (13th c.): rubble with buff/ochre render, string courses, small oculus at mid height, 2-light pointed louvred belfry opening in each face, red-brick battlemented parapet (geograph 4050912 and Manske photo). Lower west door not visible in any photo, omitted.

South elevation (street side) seen square-on in Manske's photo: coursed clunch/limestone rubble with ashlar dressings; from west: 3-light Dec traceried window in the aisle, tall 5-light window with rose/flowing tracery in the projecting south-chapel gable (centre ~14 m), smaller 3-light traceried window, pointed doorway at the east end. Replaces earlier low-confidence distant-photo annotation. Gable above eave not modelled.

East end facing Peas Hill (geograph 5524920 and 5400643, x=0 at south): south-chapel gable with tall 3-light traceried window, a smaller pointed window by the valley, chancel gable with a large blocked pointed arch containing a square-headed mullioned window, flanking chimney stack, then a low vestry with a small square window. Rubble stone with ashlar quoins; positions estimated from oblique photos.
North face of the west tower from the churchyard (geograph 4050912): ochre-rendered tower with oculus and 2-light pointed belfry opening, red-brick battlements.
